Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

people noun

persons

also persons

classical

Petr. 75.1: hominēs sumus, nōn deī
Traupman 178: Hominēs mox ejus oblīvīscentur

homō, hominis m.

noun, third declension

a person; in the plural, people

The plural hominēs is the everyday “people”.

Other words

  • mortālēs, mortālium m. pl. — people, everybody

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 1.2.175: omnēs mortālēs (Lewis & Short); Sall. Cat. 1.5 (Lewis & Short)

    Above all in omnēs mortālēs, everybody.

  • turba, turbae f. — a crowd of people

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.28: in forō turbāque (Lewis & Short)

  • populus, populī m. — a people, a nation; the public

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.39 (Lewis & Short)

    The people as a body, not persons: populus Rōmānus. Cicero defines it as nōn omnis hominum coetus quōquō modō congregātus.

Examples

  • nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī

    every one of us slips up; we’re people, not godsPetr. 75.1

  • ō quantum est hominum beātiōrum, quid mē laetius est beātiusve?

    of all the happier people there are, who is gladder or happier than me?Catull. 9.10–11

SourcesLewis & Short: homo · Lewis & Short: mortalis · Lewis & Short: turba · Lewis & Short: populus
